We introduce a probabilistic autoencoder designed to forecast future spectra for Type Ia supernovae utilizing current and past observations. By leveraging the capability of autoencoders to capture non-linear temporal dependencies, our approach extends previous research on linear correlations to non-linear domains. We train this model on a novel, self-assembled database of $1,000$ early-type supernovae (early-T Ia), comprising nearly $20$ spectra per event, to successfully forecast SDSS u-band observations with an rms reduction of $0.14$ magnitudes relative to natural variability. Furthermore, we evaluate the model's capacity to fill gaps caused by the "PS1 z-band gap"—a period of poor sensitivity for detecting early-time ejections—demonstrating that $2$ well-spaced $g$ and $z$ band observations can accurately reconstruct the full ultraviolet to optical spectrum. These findings confirm that our methodology effectively supports the analysis of data from next-generation time-domain initiatives like LSST and the Roman telescope.

We present the discovery of a resolved, neutral outflow from a dusty star-forming galaxy located at redshift $z=2.09$ and exhibiting significant gravitational lensing. By utilizing data from the VLT/MUSE integral field spectrograph, we measured the outflow's physical dimensions, velocity, and mass. Our findings indicate a highly supersonic neutral outflow with mass $M_{\rm out} = 1.2^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times 10^8\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and mean mass outflow rate $\dot{M}_{\rm out} = 1.1^{+0.6}_{-0.4}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. This outflow extends to a scale height $H_{\rm out} = 1.7\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and reaches a maximum velocity $v_{\rm out} = 1000\,\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$, yielding an outflow-to-infall mass ratio $\Psi = 1.9$. These observed values are consistent with a highly metal-enriched outflow ($Z_{\rm out}/Z_\odot = 1.9$) driven by stellar mass ($E_{\rm st}/E_{\rm grav} = 1.4$). The derived stellar mass ratio

Particle-laden plumes are ubiquitous in geophysical and engineering contexts, such as sediment-laden river outflows, mining discharge, and sediment transport. This study employs Large Eddy Simulation (LES) to investigate the entrainment dynamics of these plumes, focusing on the role of inertial effects characterized by the Newton number ($\text{We}$). Plumes were released from a circular source with fixed Reynolds number ($\text{Re}=10^4$) and particle Stokes number ($\text{St}=1$), varying the Newton number ($\text{We}$) from $0.01$ to $10$. Results indicate that both sediment-induced acceleration and fluid drag alter the structure of the source jet, with the downstream impact shifting from particle braking (at $\text{We}<1$) to fluid-dominated pushing (at $\text{We}>1$). While the entrainment rate ($\alpha$) remains constant in the initial near-field for all simulations, it increases significantly in the far-field as $\text{We}$ rises. Specifically, the enhancement stems from the kinetic energy contributed by dense particles, which amplify turbulent fluctuations and intensify the interface shear between the jet and ambient fluid.

Graphs fail to capture multi-way interactions prevalent in systems ranging from coevolution and ecological competitions to social gatherings and epidemics. Although extant spectral theories for hypergraphs have addressed basic properties, their impact on complex dynamics remains underexplored. This study introduces the use of spectral tools to analyze disease extinction within hypergraph-based populations, accounting for simultaneous multi-individual infections. Our findings establish robust lower bounds on the extinction rate, linking it to spectral properties of a specific generator. These results are applicable to various infection mechanisms and demonstrate that, conceptually, hypergraph dispersions accelerate epidemic fade-out comparable to homogeneous mixing.

The recent discovery of the two-dimensional magnetic insulator CrI₃ has attracted significant interest, particularly regarding its potential for spintronics and magnetic tunnel barriers. This study examines the spin textures of a B-type two-dimensional ferromagnetic CrI₃ bilayer using a minimal model that incorporates both magnetic anisotropy and the weak atomic-scale Rashba effect. We find that the spin textures are primarily governed by magnetic anisotropy, resulting in either a collinear configuration or a conical arrangement. Furthermore, our results indicate that neither spin polarization nor spin precession angle exhibits strong dependence on the Rashba term. These outcomes offer valuable insights into the mechanisms behind the observed collinear and conical magnetic behaviors in recent two-dimensional B-type ferromagnetic insulators.

Differential rotation serves as a primary driver of magnetic activity in solar-type stars, where the interplay between this shear and convective turbulence generates large-scale magnetic fields. In the Sun, the differential rotation peaks at equatorial latitudes and is anti-solar in the convection zone's deep regions; however, most dynamo theories assume a pro-solar profile (peaked at mid-latitudes) due to the mathematical simplicity it offers. This study investigates the consequences of incorporating a localized, anti-solar differential rotation that exists only within the outer 20% of the convection zone within dynamo frameworks. We found that such a configuration produces no significant dynamo effects in 1D models. Conversely, when included in 2D simulations, it yields a weak, quasi-stationary large-scale field lacking a clear magnetic cycle. These results suggest that sustained magnetic cycles in stars with differential rotation confined to the outer convection zone require additional complex mechanisms beyond standard mean-field dynamo processes.

Multimodal deep frameworks have become a research priority due to their ability to leverage information across diverse inputs for superior performance. Existing methods, however, are constrained by their reliance on specific input configurations, such as specific node counts or network topologies. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel Generalized K-fan (GKF) architecture. This new framework is highly adaptable, supporting variable numbers of input types and specific network structures. We evaluated the proposed GKG on several standard datasets, comparing its results against current top-performing multidimensional models. This evaluation included a comprehensive analysis of performance, per-input contributions, and internal representations. Results demonstrate that the new GKF framework not only delivers enhanced predictive accuracy but also provides deeper insights into both the contributions of distinct input types and the high-level features learned by the model.

Model verification employs automated tools to ensure the correctness of multithreaded programs by detecting bugs and ensuring compliance with specifications. Although current dominant tools depend on race conditions to bound execution, this restriction prevents the verification of programs featuring explicit state transitions or unmodeled concurrency. To address this limitation, we introduce a new verifier that leverages Dependency Graph processing to enable verification based on specific properties or properties derived from a provided model. This approach ensures minimal, precise dependency graphs, allowing for the validation of explicit checks and a defined set of possible behaviors. By enabling the specification of complex properties and delimiting behavior for better scalability, our tool was evaluated on real-world codebases. These evaluations, which included verifying explicit checks via a minimal dependency graph, demonstrated that our method effectively handles programs that previous techniques could not address.

The widespread circulation of false information on social media has prompted platforms to implement stricter policies. Specifically, it has been observed that sharing misinformation is nearly twice as frequent as distributing accurate information within the WhatsApp ecosystem. WhatsApp policy changes now prohibit users from forwarding more than five messages in a single action. This study investigates whether this limitation can effectively curb the propagation of misinformation, finding that the average number of forwarded messages concerning false claims is significantly higher than that regarding true claims. Our results indicate that limiting forward capabilities does not successfully stop the spread of misinformation; instead, it merely reduces overall message sharing without producing a noticeable decline in how misinformatio n spreads. Additionally, we identify no evidence linking the propagation of misinformation to the part of the network involving non-English speaking users.

This paper introduces a class of branching processes designed to extend the standard model of supercritical branching with two allelic frequencies. For an individual exhibiting type $A$ or type~$B$, the subsequent generation succeeds with a higher probability if the parental type is $A$. Specifically, the reproductive output for parents of type $B$ is strictly lower, resulting in a system supercritical only within the presence of type~$A$ individuals. Using analysis super-tools for the derived types of branching processes, we demonstrate that the asymptotic allelic distribution converges to a two-point distribution, where one support point corresponds to the long-run probability of the population being type~$A$ and being present, while the other corresponds to the long-run probability of the population being absent, i.e., consisting solely of type~$A$ individuals. Additionally, we derive several consequences of these results, including the determination of the expected allelic mean and variance, as well as the investigation into the expected allelic skewness.

The primary goal of spoofing detection systems is to identify synthetic artifacts within synthetic speech to effectively distinguish it from genuine human and organic speech. While contemporary state-of-the-art neural networks for spoofing detection exhibit robust performance, their reliability diminishes significantly when exposed to speech types not present in training datasets. To enhance the generalization capabilities of these models across a wider variety of speech types, we introduce a simple yet effective attentive mechanism tailored for neural network-based detection. This framework maintains compatibility with existing end-to-end detection methods, offering an improvement of up to 10.5% on difficult generalization tasks.

We develop a framework to construct global supersymmetric effective field theories (EFTs) for the inflaton, where scalar components of heavy supersymmetric fields integrate out according to standard EFT power-counting rules. Within this approach, the inflaton acts as a global symmetry that mediates between supersymmetry and the EFT describing the scalar sector. Consistency demands that the supersymmetry transformations for the inflaton and the fermionic directions corresponding to suppressed fermions vanish. Furthermore, we establish necessary conditions for the existence of supersymmetry involving the scalar potential and the Kähler metric, and demonstrate that these constraints significantly restrict how the inflaton potential evolves with respect to the inflaton field. Specifically, we show that within this framework, inflaton potentials cannot be arbitrarily chosen. As a concrete application, we verify that the two-fluid EFT model, which includes the scalar and fermionic partners of the top quark, satisfies all derived supersymmetry requirements.

Photonic systems serve as a premier platform for quantum simulations, yet physical realizations using lasers often produce asymmetrical spectra for upward transitions compared to those for downward transitions. This letter demonstrates that such generation asymmetry can significantly distort the spectral entanglement and particle correlations of quantum light. We present an asymmetry-induced modification of standard quantum correlations, creating a effective range for quantum testing. Crucially, by leveraging this asymmetry, one can ascertain the absolute frequency offset between two distinct laser sources. Experiments validating these predictions were conducted.

Superconducting quantum circuits form a prominent class within superconducting quantum computing research. Achieving quantum supremacy relies heavily on superior coherence, driven by the ability to identify and eliminate material defects that cause decoherence. This study employs Terahertz Nanoscopy (THz-NS) to investigate the heterostructure comprising a ground plane and a quantum processor made of near-coincident aluminum and silicon layers. Our findings demonstrate that near-field terahertz signals originate from two distinct mechanisms: dielectric loss within the silicon substrate and defect-induced quasiparticle excitations within the aluminum ground plane. Regarding silicon-related losses, we observe a peak in terahertz intensity above the silicon dielectric situated over via holes used for aluminum patterning. This suggests that such via structures concentrate electric field energy in the dielectric, heightening its vulnerability to loss. However, once these specific via-related mechanisms are excluded, the observed THz intensity above the aluminum ground plane correlates with defect-induced quasiparticle density. Ultimately, our work establishes near-field terahertz microscopy as a potent tool for dissecting the complex origins of decoherence in superconducting quantum processors.

Consider a real-axis Borel isomorphism $\phi\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$. We investigate the collection of all subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ satisfying two conditions: first, both $A$ and $\phi(A)$ are unions of intervals; second, the isomorphism restricts to a homeomorphism on $A$. It was previously established in a prior study that every such subset $A$ possesses the Baire property. In this paper, we demonstrate that every subset $A$ further admits a partition into pairwise disjoint non-empty open sets such that the family of constituent open sets in $\phi(A)$ mirrors exactly the family of constituent open sets in $A$ (meaning each set in the partition of $A$ corresponds one-to-one with a unique set formed by partitioning another subset of the same type under $\phi$). This resolution provides affirmative answers to two specific inquiries raised prior.

This work examines how the introduction of new, superior investment strategies impacts the profitability of persistent ones, focusing on two key variables: the tactical adjustments high-frequency traders make to existing strategies and the search for profit opportunities by agents. We employ two models: a multi-agent simulation and a single-agent approach. The single-agent model incorporates two search heuristics and one technical trading rule, alongside two additional search strategies and one technical trading rule introduced for new agents. Results reveal that all agents see their profits decline when others adopt search tactics or engage in high-frequency trading. While agents using advanced search strategies initially outperform those using only old methods, they eventually converge to similar performance levels. Our findings suggest that strategy interactions and agent behavior are critical for assessing systematic risks and investment performance, recommending the search for profit opportunities by agents and analyzing how strategies influence one another as essential steps in risk and return evaluation.

Current dynamic approaches to identify protocols using traffic‑based Netmon‑type network monitoring utilities are heavily strained by new developments. In fact, there are no dynamic methods for identifying protocols using traffic‑based Netmon‑style network monitoring utilities that can truly resist these new developments. In response, we present a set of novel attack methods designed to challenge the dynamic identification of protocols from traffic‑based open‑source network monitoring utilities. In total, we identified at least five specific attack methods: two that target the discovery of TCP handshakes, two that undermine the discovery of TCP option negotiation, and a final one that circumvents the discovery of specific IP‑v4 option negotiation.

Placing a normal metal containing Bogoliubov-de Gennes excitations and a superconductor with its own magnons into close proximity generates an effective interaction between them. This study demonstrates that effective coupling occurs specifically when the superconductor is in its chiral $p_x+ip_y$ state, leading to the formation of a composite system composed of a magnon paired with Cooper pairs. We identify that the normal metal functions as an effective gate, enabling the control of magnon propagation and density through the manipulation of electrostatic electrostatics. Furthermore, the normal metal's influence on magnon behavior is governed by its proximity to the superconductor's phase transition. These findings provide promising pathways for achieving novel hybrid devices that integrate magnons and superconducting phenomena.

Federated learning for unseen data categories is a recently emerging field. This study introduces a fresh zero-shot federated learning challenge: some participants possess training data involving new, unseen classes during the central server's global updates, while others do not. We present an Unbiased Meta-Learning (UML) approach to mitigate the negative impact of these heterogeneous data categories on model performance. Experimental results indicate that this method excels in homogeneous zero-shot scenarios compared to other meta-learning algorithms.

This paper introduces a theoretical framework for measuring all parameters of multi-qubit GHZ states in high dimensions. The core strategy involves jointly observing every qubit's polarization and an auxiliary system's energy, with the auxiliary system subsequently undergoing global quality enhancement through a specialized detector. This system enables the simultaneous observation of global quantum correlations across the entire configuration. The measured data are subsequently analyzed using the quantum optimal model to determine optimal parameter estimates and their corresponding uncertainties. As demonstrated through a $2^2$-qubit GHZ state example in current studies, this technique achieves complete measurement within approximately $2^{n-1}$ iterations for an $n$-qubit state. The proposed approach holds significant utility for advancing quantum foundations, quantum computing, and quantum information technologies.

This study introduces a channel estimation method for intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) systems. The approach utilizes a two-stage algorithm where IRS phase shifts are optimized to create a broadcast-comb-based broadcast-comb-based signal for channel estimation. The output is first processed to estimate the broad-signal characteristics, subsequently refined to estimate individual user channels. Following this estimation, phase shifts are optimized using the output. The results indicate that this two-stage method outperforms traditional single-stage weighted minimum mean-squared-error (WMMSE) algorithms, particularly in scenarios with an insufficient number of signal samples. The output is first processed to estimate the broad-signal characteristics, subsequently refined to estimate individual user channels. Following this estimation, phase shifts are optimized using the output. The results indicate that this two-stage method outperforms traditional single-stage weighted minimum mean-squared-error (WMMSE) algorithms, particularly in scenarios with an insufficient number of signal samples.

This research utilizes local news articles from NewsOwl, a crowdsourced platform covering more than 700 U.S. markets, to investigate how COVID-19 reporting connects with audience metrics, alongside case and death statistics. Using a comprehensive dataset of over 11 million articles published between March 2020 and March 2021, the study employs supervised learning to analyze the intensity of coverage relative to COVID severity and audience size while also conducting document-level sentiment analysis. The findings indicate coverage is responsive to increases in cases and deaths but remains significantly lower than pre-pandemic levels; simultaneously, the audience for such reporting fluctuates independently of pandemic metrics. These results offer essential perspectives for journalists, civic officials, and health professionals aiming to address disparities in testing and healthcare access throughout the United States.

Counting represents a fundamental yet cognitively demanding milestone in early childhood, typically emerging between the ages of two and three. While its significance is clear, the underlying cognitive process remains poorly understood. This study introduces a novel approach to representing counting as a sequential decision-making process and employs machine learning to simulate it. Specifically, we utilize a Markov decision process enhanced with a memory-augmented neural network to represent internal child cognition. The proposed system is trained via deep reinforcement learning to approximate the internal state required to acquire the counting skill automatically. The outcome is a latent cognitive model that functions as a high-capacity, structured container effectively storing essential knowledge required for counting.

Bloom filters offer a space-efficient method for quickly identifying unknown elements within a vast collection, operating with a compromise between speed and compactness. Cuckoo filters represent the subsequent advancement in this area. This paper introduces "Xor filters," a novel solution that surpasses both Bloom and Cuckoo filter approaches by delivering superior performance in terms of size and operational velocity. The proposed Xor filter combines compact address space utilization with rapid access mechanisms, achieving smaller memory footprints and reduced filter sizes while supporting constant-time additions and deletions, along with reliable failure detection.

This paper examines complex geometric views parallel to those in convex analysis. Given a convex set within a real vector space, we consider its convex enveloping functions and the resulting saddle point problems. By mapping these concepts into an algebraic geometry framework, a corresponding problem arises involving the resolution of singularities for hypersurfaces, the computation of a movable threshold for divisors, and the application of the Basepoint-Free Theorem. Finally, we delineate the relationship between solutions to both sets of problems and explore multiple generalizations of this approach within higher-dimensional real settings and across the domain of convex analysis.

This paper examines the market directional data generated from the pricing execution sequences of trades. It introduces a model to replicate transaction prices based on the information contained within the order flow. The proposed approach utilizes a non-parametric framework that does not assume specific functional forms, avoiding them entirely, to achieve price replication without imposing such constraints. The study provides impact trading strategies and pricing methods for path-dependent derivatives while also analyzing the resulting market utility. Furthermore, we present several open questions for future investigation.

Federated learning has emerged as a promising distributed machine learning paradigm, enabling multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model while retaining their local data. Although federated learning safeguards user privacy during data transfer, practical deployment faces challenges because clients often submit poorly converged models due to heterogeneous data distributions and computational constraints. Standard aggregation techniques struggle with these non-independent and non-identically distributed (NID) conditions, making robust federated learning a critical area of study. Current robust approaches are vulnerable to sophisticated attacks, notably gradient manipulation schemes like Free Lunch, which exploit optimization gaps to force specific gradient components into the global model. To address this dual challenge of vulnerability to manipulation and existing limitations in robustness, we introduce FLVoogd—a new method that integrates Voogd's concept of statistical dependency with the gradient domain for more resilient learning. Our findings demonstrate FLVoogd's superiority over competing techniques in terms of both robustness and efficiency. Additionally, the method ensures user anonymity by incorporating a codec that obfuscates user identities within submitted gradients. Comprehensive experiments across diverse real-world datasets confirm FLVoogd's significant success, specifically showing strong performance against the Free Lunch attack and surpassing the state-of-the-art free-from-download (SOTA) gradient magnitude benchmark.

This research examines the challenges of transferring learned policies from simulation to real-world scenarios within deep reinforcement learning for autonomous driving. We construct a perceptive decision-making framework where convolutional layers handle input processing and recurrent neural managed output generation. Our approach focuses on maximizing driving safety as the primary objective. To enhance generalization and real-world applicability, we implement a multi-instance training strategy that leverages varied driving simulations. Additionally, to reduce the simulation-to-real gap, we introduce gradient-based guidance during training by periodically updating model weights using data derived from actual road footage. Comprehensive evaluations indicate that our method substantially improves data efficiency and demonstrates superior capability in navigating unsimulated real environments.

Deepfake technology creates manipulative media by automatically synthesizing fake content through neural networks to spoof or falsify the identity of the subject. To mitigate this security risk, researchers have been working on detection methods and media resilience for many years. However, most previous studies have concentrated on a limited variety of file formats, often overlooking the need for robust techniques to handle a broad, unrestricted range of media types. This paper presents a comprehensive survey examining the current state of media resilience in deepfake technology, covering both generation methods and detection strategies. Additionally, we introduce a new benchmark for evaluating this resilience on a diverse set of unrestricted media. Finally, we outline open challenges in the field and suggest future research directions aimed at advancing media resilience against deepfake attacks across all forms of media.

Recent studies have identified that SH2K sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets frequently display transit variations inconsistent with H/He-dominated atmospheres, suggesting clouds formed from volatile species instead. This work introduces a new theoretical framework to explain these findings, proposing that temperate sub-Neptune planets possess oceans beneath their atmospheres, where the cloud composition results from combining gas chemistry with solubility equilibria. We develop a 1D model of the atmospheric layer above the ocean surface to simulate cloud formation and determine the composition of the subsurface ocean. Our results indicate that these worlds likely host deep oceans (reaching depths of 100s to 1000s of bars) with compositions varying by planet, featuring either water-ammonia or water-methane mixtures. Furthermore, we show that the spectral signatures of H/He can remain detectable even when obscured by clouds, provided the observable upper cloud deck maintains a high scale height due to elevated temperatures and low condensation levels. Finally, we suggest that the SH2K exoplanet population may reveal a significant fraction of these volatile-rich ocean worlds, with the current lack of gas giant counterparts in this regime potentially linked to gas giant core accretion processes.

Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer an efficient framework for spike-based computation and utilize spiking as a fundamental mechanism for learning intricate temporal patterns. Although learning in SNNs is constrained by biological realism, this limitation can be overcome by integrating teaching point neurons, which support learning through Hebbian and anti-Hebbian principles. This study investigates the capabilities of such modified SNNs by evaluating them on the synthetic Random Number Generator task and subsequent real-world datasets for emotion recognition in video and for activity classification using electrophysiological data. Results indicate that incorporating teaching point neurons significantly enhances the efficacy of SNN learning on random number generation. Similarly, on the emotion recognition task, this modification substantially boosts performance. However, for activity classification, while the adjusted SNN shows improved results, it still underperforms relative to conventional continuous Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs).

This paper introduces a new benchmark designed to assess the generalization capabilities of state-of-the-art deep neural network classifiers. By adapting and integrating multiple datasets, it constructs a "hub-and-spoke" configuration centered around a "core" dataset, with various "target" domains radiating outward. We define the "core" as ImageNet, selecting it for its extensive size, the robustness of models trained upon it, and the robustness of the resulting classifiers. Conversely, the set of target domains consists of distinct challenges that cover diverse changes in resolution, lighting, and distribution shifts. The selection of these specific domains was deliberate to create a comprehensive environment for testing generalization. The paper concludes the presentation of this new challenge by detailing the construction process and specifying the metrics used to evaluate model performance.

This study introduces an efficient approach for dynamically verifying A posteriori stochastic models based on Chaos Expansion methods using generalized (CGP). A key feature of proposed strategy is its ability to consider only a few points compared global behavior, estimating remainder term during simulation process. We compare two approaches for estimating this error: first one involves constructing deterministic bound based on model specific constraints; second utilizes statistical methods by evaluating residual statistics sample. Both strategies ensure computational efficiency while providing guarantee global control uncertainty, with extensive tests demonstrating performance.

This paper addresses a sequential identification and isolation (SICI) framework where a system's true state is only partially accessible due to random occurrences of state masking. The objective is to detect adaptive thresholds for switching systems while reliably estimating the underlying state despite these masking events. To achieve this, we develop novel limit-theorem results for the isolation and estimation processes, which then inform the design of adaptive SICI algorithms. Furthermore, we establish an almost sure asymptotic regret bound for these strategies to quantify their performance. The proposed approaches are demonstrated through their application to adaptive threshold selection in a partially obscured switching signal estimation scenario.

We investigate dwarf galaxies to explore their star formation timelines and chemical enrichment patterns, revealing that their evolutionary processes are highly variable. Although many dwarfs follow a simple model where the gas-rich initial phase ends once supernovae deplete or expel the gas below a certain stellar mass threshold, others display more intricate behaviors. These complex cases include prolonged star formation, multi-stage episodic bursts, or dwarf irregulars characterized by significant gas retention. By applying $\alpha$-enhancement patterns as a diagnostic tool, we distinguish between these different evolutionary modes. Notably, the degree of $\alpha$-enhancement provides a robust indicator of the total star formation duration, often surpassing the utility of other chemical ratios. Furthermore, we utilize the Na/M abundance ratio to probe the timing of chemical enrichment within the interstellar medium.

For any comm-ring $R$ in the category of rings with homotopy $G$-spectra, a corresponding induced action on $R\mathbf{hG}_+S$ is established. Furthermore, an $R$-module structure on $R\mathbf{H}G_+S$ via the map $GH C_+S \to RHG_+S$ yields an $RG_+S \to RHG_+S$ map that endows the latter with a compatible $G$-module structure within a tri-action of $GH C_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_+S \to RHG_

Extracting structured data from visual documents is a difficult yet vital task with broad implications for business operations worldwide. Although recent advancements in vision-language pre-training have significantly boosted the cost-effectiveness of training data for extraction models, they have unfortunately made gathering labeled data for specific business use cases nearly impossible. This study introduces a generalizable framework designed to generate highly accurate initial drafts of information using large-scale unlabeled corpora, thereby allowing labels to focus solely on correcting the pre-model's errors. By utilizing this approach to create self-correction capabilities, we demonstrate label efficiency gains of up to 90% over standard methods while sustaining, or even enhancing, extraction accuracy across various enterprise scenarios.

The interface between EuS and InAs is a critical prerequisite for constructing reliable, topologically protected quantum Hall states based on magnetic insulators combined with TxTe₂. To investigate this interface, we utilized density functional theory alongside angle- and energy-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our findings reveal that regardless of the specific linking configuration, a magnetic gap exists within the valence band structure. Furthermore, angle-resolved measurements indicate that although the InAs bulk bands shift significantly upon contact, they remain situated entirely below the top of EuS's valence band.

Although recent advancements in deep learning have yielded impressive results, the computational intensity of training these models often exceeds the capabilities of standard hardware. While the broader community has largely concentrated on developing more efficient network structures, few efforts address optimizing the training process itself. We introduce **ClickTrain**, a fine-grained, architecture-preserving method that significantly boosts both efficiency and accuracy. By dynamically detecting redundant operations and data processing steps in real-time, ClickTrain minimizes the execution of unnecessary memory reads and reads the essential data as precisely as possible. Empirical results indicate that ClickTrain outperforms state-of-the-art acceleration techniques—such as FP16, mixed precision, and tensor fusion—in delivering a 2.4× to 5.6× speedup, enabling deep learning models to train four times faster than previously possible.

We expand upon Ferri's approach to address halting issues in modal nonassociative linear logic over semilattices by incorporating modal operators. Specifically, we demonstrate how a distributive complete halting calculus for $S_4$ can be constructed as an expansion of Ferri's theory and D. Melançon and M. de Rijke's proof that $S_4$ is halting confirms that their specific axiomatic framework is likewise halting.

Neutron star–black hole (NS‑BH) mergers represent the most prevalent type of coalescing compact binary system in the universe, a population that was difficult to identify and characterize following the first detection of binary neutron star (NS‑NS) mergers by the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA (LIGO–Virgo) collaboration. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to detect gravitational waves originating from NS‑BH mergers and to classify their physical properties within the time–frequency domain. The proposed model, which we term Gravitational Wave Identification and Classification for Neutron star–Black hole (GB‑N) in our work actually stands for a specific architecture tailored for NS-BH events, is designed to operate on signal-to-noise ratios. It functions effectively on simulated detector noise and is trained using numerically generated waveforms. The framework performs two sequential operations: first, it identifies signals from NS‑BH mergers and distinguishes them from noise or other events, and second, it estimates key source parameters—including chirp mass, mass ratio, individual component masses, and spins. When applied to the full dataset of known sources from the literature, the framework achieves a detection accuracy of 99.99999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999

We report the discovery of an exoplanet, TOI-5542 b, identified via a combination of TESS photometry and ground-based radial velocity data. This system features a host star with a metallicity of [Fe/H] = -0.32 and an age estimated between 7 and 14 billion years. The discovered planet exhibits a radius of 1.11 ± 0.07 R<sub>J</sub> and a mass of 0.51 ± 0.11 M<sub>J</sub>, classifying it as a gas giant. TOI-5542 b is the first fully confirmed planet discovered around a metal-poor G-dwarf, and it is the sole known planet in such a low-metallicity population with a G-type host. Furthermore, it is the least massive planet found orbiting a G-dwarf, regardless of the host's metallicity.

We address a constrained Markov decision process and present a practical, iteration-by-step approach rooted in primal-dual theory. This method offers both theoretical and computational advantages over traditional techniques such as linear programming or the primal-dual alternating alternating direction method of multipliers, specifically demonstrating a theoretical guarantee regarding the total computational cost required to reach an $\epsilon$-optimal solution. We further validate this scheme through two examples: a path selection process on a directed graph and a multidimensional dynamic programming problem derived from a real-world application.

This paper outlines a deep learning approach to distinguishing between handwritten numbers and mathematical operators. By focusing on this specific task, the study examines characteristics of handwritten notation and develops an offset-based training strategy to enhance the separation of inputs and refine the model. The proposal also addresses the collection of operators and develops operator-specific neural networks, demonstrating that this architecture significantly outperforms models trained solely on handwritten digits.

To support this finding, we provide two distinct mathematical justifications: (1) employing the correspondence between the derived category of the projective line and the derived category of sheaves on the big complex vector space, alongside the known relationship linking the Euler forms of these categories to quantum invariants and BPS invariants respectively; and (2) utilizing the derived endomorphisms of the projective line, interpreted as the Euler forms of these categories, alongside their known

Interactions among agents in intricate networks form the basis of complex system behaviors; however, these interactions are often treated as static or randomly varying network structures, overlooking their specific temporal dynamics. This study investigates the variability of interaction processes in such networks, a factor crucial to how they shape interaction dynamics. We define interaction process variability using the stochastic duration of individual events and demonstrate that, unlike variability in random network topologies, it displays significant type-dependence on the interaction process itself. Furthermore, this variability strongly influences a wide range of outcomes, including the typical and fluctuating duration of interactions, the frequency of their repetition, and the span of the overall process.

Recent investigations into integrating Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) into reinforcement learning (RL) have demonstrated enhanced sample efficiency. This paper introduces an improved HMC-based actor-critic framework that further boosts sample efficiency. We establish the theoretical validity of our approach by deriving the specific conditions under which our model converges to an optimal policy. Additionally, although the underlying theory addresses an HMC-mean-field setting, we adapt the methodology for standard RL integration by resolving the corresponding Hamiltonian dynamics specific to policy-critical frameworks. Empirical evaluations across diverse testbeds confirm that our model not only successfully meets the intended objectives but also surpasses state-of-the-art performance.

This study introduces a robust layered navigation framework that combines visual and sonar data for real-time robot positioning. The architecture integrates a visual servo controller with a sonar-based layered navigation system, allowing the robot to merge information from multiple sensors to determine its location efficiently. Experimental results validate the proposed method, demonstrating enhanced robustness in the navigation process.

Pluto's New Horizons flyby revealed that icy blends of water ice and organic materials dominate the surfaces of the dwarf planet Pluto and its largest moons, Charon and Nereid. While the 2020 MAST observations from Space-based Infrared Telescope (MIRI) provided initial spectral evidence for such mixtures on Nereid, this study leverages higher-resolution NIR data from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) to refine those constraints. We modeled Nereid's reflectance spectra using a radiative transfer code, testing mixtures of water ice with various organics (thiophene, tholin, tholin, and hydrocarbon). Our analysis indicates a preference for tholin-rich compositions over hydrocarbon-rich ones, suggesting a composition roughly 50% tholin and 50% water ice by volume. Although we acknowledge that atmospheric deposition could alter the spectral interpretation, our geometric albedo constraints suggest Nereid's current, non-atmospheric atmosphere is inconsistent with extensive global surface deposits of tholins.

Let $T_n(K)$ denote the subset of all $n \times n$ lower triangular matrices within $M_n(K)$ that share a specific idempotent property. Consequently, $T_n(K)$ forms a structure that is not a ring but a locally ring, which is important for the study of certain geometric configurations in linear algebra. This article demonstrates that the affine plane consisting of all ordered $n$-tuples of elements from $T_n(K)$, denoted as $AT_n$, corresponds exactly to the affine plane $\mathcal{T}_n$ composed of all idempotent matrices within $T_n(K)$ that are lower triangular. Similarly, it proves that the projective plane defined by one-dimensional right $T_n(K)$-modules is equivalent to the projective plane $\mathcal{P}_n$ made up of all idempotent matrices within $T_n(K)$ that are lower triangular.

The principle $\ulcorner J_1^\zeta \rrull$ (for relevant countable ordinals $\ulcorner \zeta \rrull$) serves as an extension of Tarski's finite model theory axiom, which asserts that every infinite set can be placed in a Tukey maximum order. While Shelah demonstrated that this principle follows from large cardinal axioms specifically stronger than those required to derive Martin's Axiom, it remains unknown if it holds within models of $\neg CH$ (the negation of the Continuum Hypothesis). This note addresses this gap by presenting two models satisfying $\neg CH$ in which $\ulcorner J_1^\zeta \rrull$ fails. The first instance arises from adding $\omega_2$ random reals to a ground model, while the second features the Easton support iteration of GCH.

This paper addresses the creation of optimal dynamic treatment regimes for patients with chronic conditions by employing a multi-period, multi-cohort, Bayesian learning framework. This approach facilitates the simultaneous optimization of treatment strategies for diverse patient groups and enables simultaneous learning across them. By utilizing a flexible non-parametric prior for the treatment response function, we ensure adaptability to various underlying data structures. Furthermore, we propose a novel metric called "negativity" to assess clinical harm, which serves as a foundational element for our proposed "negative optimization" objective for defining these regimes.

We introduce a new class of presheves defined on the category of finite sets and bijections, demonstrating that this class encompasses all presheves obeying the stabilisation map standard in arithmetic presheheing. Our primary finding establishes a duality for these newly defined presheheing, an result that generalises the known duality found within $A^1$-homological homological dualities. As a specific application, we derive the corresponding STL (stabilisation, transfer, localisation) theorem and provide an alternative proof of the Hodge decomposition theorem for the Lubin-Tate formal group.

Superconductivity in topological materials often stems from the pairing of quasiparticles residing on reduced-dimensional surfaces or edges. In contrast, this work identifies and characterizes three-dimensional many-body mechanisms that enable direct superconducting pairing within bulk bulk topological phases associated with smooth band structures. We formulate an analytical framework for the corresponding two-body interaction potentials and demonstrate the existence of stable two-quasiparticle bound states through rigorous many-body calculations employing both a standard Hubbard model and a recently identified topological lattice phase featuring smooth bands.

For a locally compact abelian group $G$, Polya established in 1928 that any two subgroups sharing the same topological dimension and satisfying $\widehat{G}$ being a torsion group are equivalent (isomorphic) if and only if they share an image isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^n$. This work extends that theorem to demonstrate that for two subgroups $H$ and $K$ of a locally compact abelian group $G$ with $\dim_H = \dim_K = 1$ and $\widehat{G}$ a torsion group provided that $H/\overline{H}$ and $K/\overline{K}$ are both torsion, then $H$ and $K$ are isomorphic if and only if there exists an automorphism of $G$ mapping $H$ onto a subgroup of $K$.

Presence-absence data is frequently encountered in ecological and evolutionary research, yet standard clustering techniques often yield suboptimal results on such data, particularly in high-dimensional contexts. This study evaluates various clustering approaches, including standard methods and those tailored for presence-absence data, using a simulation framework based on a latent Gaussian process with a Dirichlet-multinomial observation model. This model accommodates arbitrary correlation structures, allowing for both spatial and non-spatial scenarios as well as spatial-temporal combinations. Findings indicate that a modified entropy clustering approach, applied to edited input data, is the most reliable in terms of accuracy and consistency across all three conditions—spatial, non-spatial, and spatial-temporal—regarding both spatial and spatio-temporal settings.

Salient object detection focuses on identifying the main content within an image, with applications ranging from image editing and indexing to medical image analysis. While numerous methods exist, most depend heavily on manual tuning of parameters, which limits their adaptability across diverse images and reduces their automation potential. We introduce a comprehensive, unified framework capable of processing both RGB and RGB-D inputs to identify and locate key objects. By integrating multiple cues and leveraging both spatial and temporal information, our strategy offers enhanced robustness and consistency. A key contribution is an entirely automatic method for establishing a necessary salient object training database, eliminating the need for manual annotations. We further present a unified model designed for accurate salient object detection using either RGB or combined RGB-D data. Experimental results demonstrate that temporal information significantly boosts detection accuracy, with our algorithm outperforming contemporary methods on standard RGB and RGB-D benchmarks.

This study outlines the UM-Iu@LING entry for SemEval-2019 Task 6 (Identifying Aggressive Sentences). We developed a hybrid architecture combining a bidirectional BERT model with a support vector machine (SVM), trained exclusively on the provided training set data. Evaluated across three subtasks, this model achieved the highest scores in the combined (subtask 1+2) track and ranked second overall.

A palindromic number reads the same forwards and backwards, such as 7, 11, or 22. For a non-palindromic positive integer $n$ with $l(n)$ representing the number of its digits, we define $Q(n)$ as the smallest positive integer $q$ such that $n \cdot q$ results in a palindromic number. Consider the set $K$ containing all integers that cannot be expressed as $Q(n)$ for any $n$. This paper investigates the distribution of the quotient function $Q(n)$ and analyzes the density of the set $K$.

Multislice detectors enable the acquisition of polyenergetic X-ray projections, which, though detrimental to image quality compared to monoenergetic ones, facilitate enhanced reconstruction and precise quantification of physical properties like effective atomic number and mass density through material decomposition. Achieving accurate results with polyenergetic data requires simultaneous consideration of energy-dependent characteristics for image formation, the calibration-induced noise floor on sensors, and the specific materials' response. To address this, we propose a nonsplit variational approach that jointly performs denoising of polyenergetic sensors and reconstruction/reconstruction-quantification for polyenergetic CT. Experiments utilizing simulated polyenergetic datasets confirm that our method yields high-fidelity reconstructions and precise material quantification while effectively removing sensor noise.

Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) faces significant challenges due to its reliance on extensive training data, particularly for underrepresented low-resource languages. While few-shot learning offers a promising solution by enabling effective recognition from minimal examples, it has previously been underutilized in handwritten recognition. This paper presents the first large-scale application of few-shot learning to HTR, demonstrating its efficacy across both high- and low-capacity languages. By employing a novel sequence-to-sequence deep learning model and applying a one-shot data generation strategy, we achieve an average character error rate reduction of 23.1% in 14 high-resource languages and up to 33.8% in three 2-language resources, all using only 14 training samples. Additionally, we introduce a synthetic data creation method that leverages visual similarities between character graphs to enhance performance. Experiments indicate that this data generation approach significantly boosts one-shot accuracy in both high- and low-resource languages, delivering up to a 12.8% CE improvement in 2-language resources when using 14 training samples.

The first method employs a "many-body localized" strategy, extending the success of the spectral function approach—previously validated for lighter masses up to $A \leq 40$—to heavier systems. The second integrates the "mean-field in the shell model" method, a hybrid framework that functions as an interpolation between traditional shell model and mean-field theories. Topological insulators and semimetals represent a fascinating frontier in condensed matter physics, recently prompting the creation of various teaching resources aimed at undergraduate students in science and engineering. This paper serves as one such material, outlining fundamental principles of band theory and quantum mechanics essential for understanding topological quantum phenomena, with a specific focus on an effective two-band model. By progressing from basic to sophisticated concepts and demonstrating their relevance within topological contexts through the exploration of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, an effective Hamiltonian is developed before analyzing its properties. These properties are further validated by examining edge states in finite SSH chains and observing phase-dependent spectra in infinite systems, with all calculations performed using Python and its NumPy library. Finally, the accompanying Python scripts and additional pedagogical aids are made publicly accessible online.

It is proven that any composition operator arising from a composition pair involving a map $\psi$ directed into a unit-distance diameter convex domain $\psi$ mapping into a unit-distance diameter convex domain $\psi$ must be compact. We employ standard quantum field theory techniques to compute the two-loop effective potential for a supermultiplication of three-forms and demonstrate its equivalence to the AdS5xS5 superstring background effective potential. This result confirms the matching of the corresponding quantum corrections arising from the effective field theory of three-forms and the low-energy string theory effective field equations. In addition, our findings establish the consistency of AdS5xS7 three-form supergravity with previous high precision string theory calculations.

Object-oriented programming languages are widely adopted for developing applications that leverage the massive parallel processing capabilities of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). Nevertheless, existing GPU memory allocators are optimized for structurally distinct patterns and fail to effectively manage the complex layouts inherent to object-based code. Furthermore, current solutions neglect critical aspects such as GPU cache efficiency and the variability in pointer arithmetic widths. This study introduces **DynaSOAr**, a novel unified memory allocator designed specifically for object-oriented environments on GPUs. DynaSOAr achieves superior performance by aggregating contiguous memory for similar objects to minimize access latency, allocating precise amounts based on data-type size to eliminate wasted space, and organizing the allocation header to optimize cache usage. Benchmark results indicate that dynasoar delivers competitive execution times and reduces memory access times by a factor of 2.5x to 3.5x, while slash allocations—saving 50% to 70% of unnecessary memory—are observed in these scenarios.

We examine three $U(1)_X$ models defined within $SO(10)$ grand unified theory, each incorporating a $U(1)_X$ gauge boson alongside five right-handed neutrinos. Our analysis focuses on the mass spectrum of right-handed neutrinos and the subsequent lightest neutral lepton mass resulting from electroweak symmetry breaking. We evaluate whether the right-handed seesaw mechanism can effectively account for the observed light mass of the right-handed neutral lepton in each model. Additionally, we explore the implications for the decay of the right-handed neutral lepton into right-handed neutral fermions and compare these theoretical predictions with experimental data regarding the right-handed decay channels of the right-handed leptons.

Biomechanical investigations into hollow organs, such as the aorta, frequently involve subjecting a cane surrogate to internal pressure to replicate the effect of blood flow. While prior research has established a direct correlation between pressure-induced dilation and the development of axial shortening, there is a lack of understanding regarding the mechanical stability of the cane model itself. This study derives equations for both the length and the radius of a pressurized tube to predict the resulting shortening and widening, validating these equations against experimental data with high precision. Furthermore, we analyze the structural stability of the model, demonstrating that although it qualitably mimics the arterial system, it exhibits a distinct shortcoming: unlike arteries, a specifically pressurized cane tube can reach a state of mechanical instability under certain conditions.

Integrity in AI decision-making is paramount, particularly when deep learning models are deployed in high-stakes environments where assurance of correct behavior is required under uncertain conditions. We introduce a novel approach to guarantee robustness in AI systems by applying credally probabilistic reasoning to identify and prevent erroneous outcomes. Our method constructs large-scale credal Bayesian networks to model uncertainty and uncertainty about system states, utilizing a scalable algorithm based on structural properties of probabilistic circuits for circuit evaluation. This technique empowers engineers to certify robustness by ensuring no unacceptable outcomes are possible under any variant of the model. We demonstrate the applicability and performance of this approach through a case study on a critical decision-making scenario involving emergency room triage for patients presenting with chest pain.

We introduce a phononic analog to electron Bloch oscillations by driving phononic crystals through a moving boundary. A resonant response emerges when the excitation frequency matches the ratio of the applied mechanical excitation frequency and the lattice's spatial frequency. This phenomenon demonstrates an acoustic version of dynamical diffraction, enabling the detection of unit-cell scales and standing wave patterns via this resonance. Consequently, this mechanism offers a new method for characterizing phononic crystals and provides access to the semiclassical regime of their dynamics.

In a generalized quadrangle $(\mathcal{Q},\mathcal{S})$, a code $\mathcal{C}$ is defined as $s$ neighbor-transitive if the permutation representation of the automorphism group $\Gamma=\Gamma(\mathcal{Q})$ restricted to $\mathcal{C}$ yields a transverse action on the $\s$-neighborhood of any codeword. This article presents four instances of such codes that are not equivalent under equivalence relations defined by isometry. The first three examples correspond to maximal partial spreads where no two lines are incident, whereas the fourth represents a collection of mutually maximal partial spreads where some pairs are indeed incident. These three non-incident cases correspond to specific generalized quadrangles with known line counts of 56, 308, and 196 respectively.

The central molecular zone (CMZ) of the Milky Way exhibits a highly complex and extreme environment, characterized by dense gas, powerful radiation, and strong gravitational fields. To better understand the structure and dynamics of this region, we employed the 2D correlation function to analyze high-resolution ($\sim$0.3 pc) dust emission maps of the inner 100 pc obtained from Herschel/PACS surveys. Our analysis reveals that the dust emissivity anisotropies at scales of approximately 100 pc are significant, with peak values reaching a maximum of $f_{max} = 1.24$ within a directional angle of $\theta = 44^\circ$. These findings indicate that the alignment of dust grains is strongly influenced by galactic magnetic fields, suggesting that the dust grain alignment in the CMZ is highly anisotropic.

We have developed a nonlinear, multi-exponential rate model to explain the dynamics of core-electron populations following the core hole creation in gas-phase molecules by intense X-ray pulses. In this framework, various electronic states—including core-excited, core-ionized, and photoexcited configurations—are linked to specific rate processes, while electron movement among states via Coulomb interaction is represented by a set of coupled differential equations. These equations were resolved numerically for core-ionization events in hydrogen chloride ($\text{ClH}$) using experimentally measured photoionization cross-sections to define initial population distributions for core-ionized, core-excited, and various photoexcited states. By fitting model parameters to available transient absorption data, we achieved excellent agreement between simulated and experimental results for core-ionized states with multiple occupancy levels, as well as for core-excited states. Furthermore, by employing a simplified configuration interaction approach to estimate energy shifts induced by core-hole screening, our model successfully accounts for the significant nonlinearity observed in high-fluence absorption spectra, specifically predicting both the $9$ eV spectral shift and the concomitant reduction in core-excited population.

This study introduces a low-power, inaccuracy temperature sensor designed for on-chip monitoring of integrated circuits. Leveraging a self-calibrated approach, the sensor achieves a compact footprint of 0.0015mm² with power consumption as low as 1.06nJ per conversion. It operates across a wide supply range of 0.6V to 1.8V, delivering a resolution of 0.24{\deg}C and outperforming prior art by reducing silicon area by 86.6%, power consumption by 66.6%, and inaccuracy by 33.3%.

We introduce a novel method to generate polarization entanglement between two photons, guided by the "quantum scissors" framework, by utilizing spatial modes with diverse spatial diversity factors. This approach eliminates the need for auxiliary auxiliary entanglement or complex optical components like beam splitters or polarizing beam directors. By manipulating the power ratios of these spatial modes relative to one another, we can both generate entangled states and optimize their fidelity. The validity of our methodology is confirmed through simulation results, which demonstrate the ability to produce the highest fidelity entanglement by generating the W-state when the system operates under conditions of limited auxiliary entanglement.

We introduce the concept of digital Euclidean spanners, adapting standard $(k, \epsilon)$-spanner definitions to the grid environment where spanners exist. A digital spanner exists on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ relative to a specific spanness function if there is a designated set of $\epsilon$-round, $\epsilon$-convex balls of radius. For this topology to qualify, there must exist a set of these balls that collectively form a $(k, \epsilon)$-spanner, where the maximum distance between any two such balls is no larger than the ball count in that spanner. In the case of dimension one ($d=1$), there exists an infinite family of such digital spanners. On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and higher dimensions ($d \geq 2$), however, these families do not exist for any fixed $\epsilon$. Furthermore, we establish that any digital $(k, \epsilon)$-spanner on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ must have a size complexity of at least $\Omega((k/\epsilon)^{d-1})$. Specifically, for $\mathbb{Z}^2$, there exists a barrier preventing the existence of a $(k, \epsilon)$-spanner with fewer than $\Omega(k^2)$ edges.

Machine learning (ML) techniques have proven highly effective across numerous classification challenges, including identifying devices within an ecosystem. While cost-conscious feature selection methods exist to reduce the computational expenses of ML algorithms, current IoT-specific cost-oriented approaches are scarce. This study presents an investigation into costs associated with individual features within device contexts and introduces a novel algorithm for constructing feature subsets specifically tailored to IoT ecosystem discovery. The method leverages contextual features and utilizes context as a proxy for estimation to minimize the costs of ecosystem detection. Validated against the real-world dataset from the CoSDI project, this approach demonstrates superior performance compared to standard ML algorithms, achieving higher accuracy with significantly lower computational overhead.

This study extends previous research by S. A. Grädel and the present authors to investigate Gödel modal logics derived from Tarski's intuitionistic propositional logic over finite chains, specifically focusing on Gödel algebras that correspond to these reasoning systems. We establish characterizations involving both relational structures and syntactic term algebras for both solid and general contexts. Furthermore, our results explore the homomorphic images of solid Gödel algebras as well as congruences within the broader category. To support these findings, specific examples of relevant Gödel algebras are analyzed. Additional work addresses the structural properties of topologies on prime spectra for these logic systems and defines concepts of definability and computability concerning term definitions within them.

We introduce a novel approach to real-time word alignment designed to handle both intractable monolingual datasets and scenarios involving word alignment within specific domains. By leveraging shared knowledge between such data types, our method successfully transfers patterns from extensive monolingual sources to targeted alignment tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate through both theoretical analysis and empirical results that the utilization of monolingual data significantly enhances performance on complex multilingual tasks.

This study introduces a proposed algorithm designed to generate Nash equilibria in finite non-convonic games using the distorted resolvent approach to solve the associated variational inequality. By modifying an external perturbation at each iteration, the method ensures that the generated sequence remains finite, preventing cyclic behavior. This strategic modification also guarantees $\Delta$-convergence of the iterates to a solution of the variational inequality. Furthermore, the paper establishes a connection between the iterations produced by this algorithm and those of the standard resolvent method, demonstrating that our proposed method's output constitutes a subsequence of sequences generated by a broader class of resolvent algorithms.

We have implemented a suite of calculations relevant to Primordial Black Hole (PBH) dark matter models within the astrophysical modeler ModelSim (specifically, Model SIPYCL E) to facilitate PBH research. This work model includes modeling accretion of PBHs in an $\Lambda$CDM universe with varying parameters, as well as determining PBH abundance from various constraints such as microlensing, PBH evaporation, dynamical effects on compact objects, and CMB anisotropies. The output of this model is used to investigate the parameter space of interest to the scientific community.

We investigate the statistical mechanics of hard convex polygons that randomly tile the plane. In our model, a configuration consists of a point process where each point is associated with a polyhedron, and all such arrangements conflicting with each other's space are excluded. Focusing on equilateral triangles and squares with uniform selection, we employ advanced numerical techniques to map the phase diagram, revealing an disordered phase alongside two crystalline states: a triangular lattice and a square lattice. Crucially, our analysis demonstrates that the intervening disordered region exhibits splay-type modulation in its metric correlations, a signature that distinguishes it from the nematic crystallization observed in traditional liquid crystal models.

Stagnant and aperiodic random fields on a sphere, characterized by specified mean and covariance structures, find applications in diverse domains such as geophysics, geology, and cosmology. This study derives recurrence relations for the Hermite-Chebyshev-Polychronopoulos (HCP) coefficients of these fields. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on step-by-step (multi-step) recurrence methods, our proposed technique calculates the field coefficients directly. Furthermore, we establish connections between these HCP coefficients and Neumann–Cohen spherical covariance functions, as well as their correlations with the coefficients of spherical harmonic coefficients.

Spectator imaging, also known as interaction-free imaging, allows imaging without direct particle interaction between the probe and the object being imaged. While the original approach relied on single-particle interference from coherent sources, this work demonstrates a spectator imaging technique using an intensity-correlation protocol with a single photon. This method achieves single-pixel imaging at the quantum limit, offering distinct advantages by eliminating interference stability requirements and correlating image intensity directly with probability.

The complex flow behavior of highly viscous, disordered liquids, such as colloidal suspensions and granular pastes, is significantly shaped by friction. This study examines the relationship between friction and flow dynamics in quasi-two-dimensional foams, revealing a strong correlation between local flow velocity and the thermodynamic state of the foam. By employing an original technique to measure local yield stress, we identified that this metric strongly correlates with the local yield stress of the system. Our findings indicate that the coexistence of high yield stress and high viscosity results in a characteristic "textured" structure. Consequently, we propose a simple model that successfully reproduces the experimentally observed non-local effects, specifically the emergence of vortex-like structures within the flow field.

This paper presents a hybrid approach combining the Inception and DenseNet deep learning architectures for diagnosing skin cancer, supplemented by outlier detection to identify atypical cases. Since standard neural networks assume all training data belongs to a single class distribution, they struggle with samples that deviate from this norm. We employ a dedicated outlier detection mechanism because incorporating non-conforming data can mislead conventional classifiers. Specifically, we utilize an autoencoder to construct a denoising layer that identifies multivariate outliers by measuring reconstruction error.

We have measured the non-linear optical response of solid sodium, an almost-free electron metal, to continuous-wave laser radiation. By examining the response both with and without DC fields, we determined that electronic quasi-particles possess lifetimes ranging from 10 to 100 femtoseconds. These findings imply a relaxation time for momentum significantly longer than what is predicted by standard nearly-free electron metal theory.

This paper presents a new approach to irreversibly expand a system's phase space, a step essential for generating Phasespace Monte Carlo (PSMC) ensembles that exceed the traditional NVT constraint. By employing a continuous free expansion in configuration space, the method irons out local minima and accentuates the system's available states. Implemented within a PSMC framework, the technique allows for sampling configurations from novel ensemble distributions, a goal achieved by integrating the continuous expansion with a continuous reverse contraction process. The reverse contraction restores the system to the NVT ensemble, a transition facilitated by the variable number of particles configuration created during the expansion. The study demonstrates the method's efficacy through two simulations: water monomers, which serve to refine the expansion parameters for optimal performance, and the Lennard-Jones fluid, where the method significantly enhances sampling efficiency compared to standard PSMC techniques.

We perform explicit computations of the coefficients for kongevich's polynomials related to deformation quantization of symplectic structures, with a focus on graphs constructed from moment connections and curvatures. This study introduces a novel approach for calculating nanoptera—a class of unstable, nonlocal, homoclinic orbits characterized by exponentially small oscillations—within two specific granular chains: a theoretical weakly nonlinear "timber" chain and a specific diatomic chain based on experimental parameters. For both systems, an adaptive weak-nonlinear approximation scheme is applied, utilizing a generalized weak-nonlinear resonance equation to which a KAM-type nondegeneracy condition is imposed. By enforcing this condition and addressing global dynamics, the research establishes the presence of nanoptera in both models. Consequently, the findings suggest the persistence of these trajectories in the fully nonlinear regimes, with implications for related structures such as solitary waves, breathers, and granites.

We investigate how physics specific to an intermediate mass scale influences primordial power spectra and higher-order correlation functions (primitves) during inflation. Our model posits that an $SU(2)$ gauge theory becomes conformal at high scales and breaks via a discrete symmetry at lower energies. We demonstrate that features imprinted on the power spectra and correlation structures from this intermediate mass scale remain pristine and detectable, even in noisy, higher-statistic data. Specifically, we focus on estimating the signal-to-noise ratio for distinct cosmological collider signatures. These signals include the $1st$-excited state triplet within the quadrupole channel of inflationary collider observables and the associated momentum-dependent structure factor known as a "bead." Our findings indicate that despite the noise inherent in such estimates, the underlying features linked to the intermediate mass scale offer a robust and reliable means of extracting these vital cosmological signals.

We investigate the dynamical evolution of a quantum two-state vector, applying a periodic control field to its components. This system generalizes the well-established three-color Raman atom-light interaction framework into a broader context. Our findings reveal that the dynamics obey global, universal scaling laws. Specifically, we demonstrate that the time evolution can be partitioned into a rapid initial phase and a subsequent slower stage. During this secondary phase, the system exhibits a distinct sub-cycling behavior with a period exactly three times the driving field's period. Furthermore, we locate and characterize an energy spectrum associated with this effective Hamiltonian in the $2 \times 2$ space, which fully explains the system's long-term behavior. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical foundation for understanding three-state quantum walks and similar two-qubit interactions driven by periodic fields.

Vision Transformers (ViTs) have recently achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous computer vision benchmarks, surpassing convolutional neural networks (CNNs). In unsupervised settings, methods like Swin-Transformer- Large (SWIN-L) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities. This study investigates the intrinsic learning mechanisms of these self-supervised transformers by analyzing them through linear classifiers and visualizing class centers alongside feature embeddings using t-SNE. Our qualitative findings indicate that these models acquire robust semantic hierarchies, similar to supervised approaches, yet they also develop additional attributes with distinct functional roles. Through quantitative analysis of individual ViT layers and attention distributions, we observed that lower layers tend to capture high-frequency details, whereas higher layers focus on low-frequency information. We propose that this hierarchical processing supports semantic clustering, while the acquisition of emergent properties likely stems from the transformer's ability to effectively model long-range dependencies. Finally, we assessed the impact of these emergent attributes on performance when adapted to downstream tasks. Results show that using them enhances downstream accuracy compared to pure semantics, suggesting that these properties act as effective inductive biases that facilitate better generalization.

Our analysis indicates that this dark matter fluid experiences friction due to interactions with dark energy, resulting in an accelerated expansion of space. We formulate a dissipative dark substance model constrained by a friction term proportional to the velocity of the expansion. The components of the energy-momentum tensor for this substance are derived, and the corresponding field equations are expanded in terms of the scale factor's derivatives with respect to the square, an expansion known as the first LTB-series. Our examination of the physical feasibility of this model demonstrates that the proposed dark matter fluid satisfies the weak, dominant, and LTB forms of stability conditions.
